title: Kept together or kept apart
objectives: Count arrangements with items kept together by gluing them into a block.
Count arrangements with items kept apart as everything minus together.
Count seatings round a table by fixing one seat.

screens.title: Kept together or kept apart
screens.prose: Seating plans come with rules: these two must sit together, those two must not. We will count both kinds of plan without listing them.
Ana, Ben and Cal (A, B and C) sit at three desks in a row. The grid lists all $3! = 6$ seatings, read left to right. Tap a cell to select it.
screens.question: Tap every seating where Ana and Ben sit side by side.

hints.text: Side by side means no one sits between them.
In this seating Cal sits between Ana and Ben.
The pair can be AB or BA. Cal sits on its left or its right.

feedback.correct: Four of the six seatings keep Ana and Ben together.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Shade each seating with A and B next to each other, either way round.

byKey.one-way: You found the seatings with Ana on Ben's left. Ben can also sit on Ana's left: BAC and CBA.
byKey.r1c2: In ACB, Cal sits between Ana and Ben.
byKey.r2c1: In BCA, Cal sits between Ben and Ana.

explain.text: Four seatings keep them together: ABC, BAC, CAB and CBA. The pair sits on the left or the right, and faces AB or BA. That is $2 \times 2 = 4$.

screens.prose: Dev (D) joins, so there are 24 seatings. Picture Ana and Ben taped together as one block. Tap a cell to select it, and tap again to clear it.
screens.question: Tap every seating that contains the block AB, with Ana directly left of Ben.

hints.text: Look for the letters A and B touching, in that order.
ABCD starts with the block. Where else does AB appear?

feedback.correct: Six seatings contain AB: the block, Cal and Dev in $3! = 6$ orders.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Shade only the seatings where the letters AB touch, in that order.

byKey.both-ways: You also shaded the BA seatings. Those have the block facing the other way. Keep only AB for now.
byKey.r2c1: There Ben sits directly left of Ana: that is the block BA. Keep only AB for now.
byKey.r2c2: There Ben sits directly left of Ana: that is the block BA. Keep only AB for now.
byKey.r3c3: There Ben sits directly left of Ana: that is the block BA. Keep only AB for now.
byKey.r3c6: There Ben sits directly left of Ana: that is the block BA. Keep only AB for now.
byKey.r4c3: There Ben sits directly left of Ana: that is the block BA. Keep only AB for now.
byKey.r4c6: There Ben sits directly left of Ana: that is the block BA. Keep only AB for now.

explain.text: Six seatings contain AB: the block, Cal and Dev are 3 units in $3! = 6$ orders. Flipping the block to BA gives 6 more. So $3! \times 2! = 12$ seatings keep Ana and Ben together.

screens.prose: Eve (E) joins, so five traders sit in a row. Ana and Ben must sit together. **Gluing** them into one block leaves 4 units to arrange, and the block faces 2 ways.
screens.question: How many seatings keep Ana and Ben together?

hints.text: How many units are there once Ana and Ben are glued?
This block can read AB or BA.
$4!$ orders of the units, times $2!$ ways for the block.

feedback.correct: $4! = 24$ orders of the units, each with the block either way round.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Arrange the 4 units, then multiply by the ways the block can face.

byKey.one-way: You arranged the 4 units but kept the block as AB. It can also face BA, which doubles the count.
byKey.all: That is every seating of five, $5!$. Many of those split Ana and Ben.
byKey.five-units: You multiplied $5!$ by 2. Once glued, there are 4 units, not 5.

explain.text: The 4 units go in $4! = 24$ orders, and each order has the block either way round. So $4! \times 2! = 48$ seatings keep them together.

screens.prose: Six traders now: Ana to Eve, and Fay (F). Ana, Ben and Cal form the rates desk and must sit as a group of three, in any order.
screens.question: How many seatings keep the three together?

hints.text: Glue the three into one block. How many units are left?
Inside this block, the three can sit in any order.
$4! \times 3! = 24 \times 6$.

feedback.correct: $4!$ orders of the units, times $3!$ orders inside the block.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Arrange the units, then arrange the three inside their block.

byKey.one-way: You arranged the units but kept the block in one order. Three people inside it have $3! = 6$ orders.
byKey.pair: You multiplied by $2!$, as for a pair. The block holds three people, so it has $3!$ orders.
byKey.all: That is every seating of six, $6!$. Most of those split the rates desk.

explain.text: Gluing leaves 4 units in $4! = 24$ orders. Inside the block the three sit in $3! = 6$ orders. So there are $24 \times 6 = 144$ seatings.

screens.prose: Back to five traders, Ana to Eve. Ana and Ben have fallen out, so they must not sit side by side.
screens.question: How many seatings keep Ana and Ben apart?

hints.text: Every seating has Ana and Ben either together or apart.
You counted the together seatings on an earlier screen: 48.
All seatings minus the together ones: $5! - 48$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all seatings, then take away the ones that keep Ana and Ben together.

byKey.together: That is the together count. The question asks for the seatings that split them.
byKey.all: That is every seating. Take away the 48 that keep Ana and Ben together.
byKey.one-way: You took away 24, the block facing one way only. The together count is 48.

explain.text: Every seating keeps them together or apart, never both. So apart is everything minus together: $120 - 48 = 72$. Counting what you do not want, then subtracting, is the next lesson's main tool.

screens.title: Round a table
screens.prose: Five traders sit at a round table with identical chairs. Moving everyone one seat round gives the same seating: everyone keeps the same neighbours on each side. The two tables show the same seating.

state.caption: Left: one seating, clockwise from the top. Right: everyone has moved one seat round.

screens.question: How many different seatings are there?

hints.text: Write a seating as a row, starting from any chair. How many rows give the same round seating?
Sit Ana down first. Her chair becomes the reference point.
With Ana fixed, the other four fill the chairs clockwise from her in $4!$ ways.

feedback.correct: Fix Ana, then arrange the other four: $4! = 24$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each round seating can be read as a row starting from any of its 5 chairs.

byKey.row: You counted the rows, $5!$. Each round seating appears 5 times among them, once for each turn of the table.
byKey.mirror: You also treated mirror images as the same. A mirror image swaps everyone's left and right neighbours, which is a new seating.
byKey.minus-one: You took away 1 for the repeat. Each seating repeats 5 times among the rows, so divide by 5.

explain.text: Each round seating shows up 5 times among the $5! = 120$ rows, once per turn of the table. So there are $\tfrac{5!}{5} = 4! = 24$. Fixing Ana's chair and arranging the other four gives the same $(5-1)!$.

screens.prose: A different dinner. Now the round table has numbered place cards, and the plan says who sits in which numbered seat.

state.caption: Each node shows a seat number, then who sits there. On the right, everyone has moved one seat round.

screens.question: How many different seating plans are there now?

options.why: You divided by 5 for the turns of the table. With numbered seats, a turn moves everyone to a new number, so it is a new plan.
You multiplied by 5 turns of the table. The $5!$ already puts each person in each numbered seat.
You divided for turns and for mirror images. Numbered seats make every plan different.

hints.text: Compare the two tables. Is Ana in the same numbered seat?
Seat 1 holds Ana on the left and Eve on the right.
Five different seats and five people: fill seat 1, then seat 2, and so on.

feedback.correct: Numbered seats are five different places, so all $5! = 120$ plans differ.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask whether turning everyone one seat round changes the plan.

byKey.rotations: You divided by 5 for the turns of the table. With numbered seats, a turn moves everyone to a new number, so it is a new plan. Divide only when the seats are alike.

explain.text: Turns of the table only repeat a seating when the seats are alike. Numbered seats are five different places, so this is a row of 5 bent into a circle: $5! = 120$.

screens.prose: We want a formula for $n$ people in a row with Ana and Ben apart. Check it against your 72 for $n = 5$.
screens.question: Put the lines of the argument in order.

lines.text: All $n$ people in a row: $n!$ seatings.
Glue Ana and Ben: $n - 1$ units, in $(n-1)!$ orders.
The block faces 2 ways, so $2\,(n-1)!$ seatings keep them together.
Each seating is together or apart, so apart $= n! - 2\,(n-1)!$.

hints.text: Start with the count that has no rule at all.
The together count needs both the glue and the flip before you can subtract.
All, glue, flip, subtract, then tidy with $n! = n\,(n-1)!$.

feedback.correct: Everything, then the together count, then subtract and tidy.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Build the together count before you subtract it.

byKey.factor: The tidy form comes from the subtraction, so it goes last.

explain.text: Apart is everything minus together, and together is glue then flip. Taking out the common factor gives $(n-2)\,(n-1)!$, which is 72 for five traders.

screens.prose: A desk ranks five traders, Ana to Eve, by monthly P&L. Ana and Ben both made exactly £12,500.00, so they tie and share a place. The other three P&Ls all differ.

state.caption: Four places to rank: the tie, Cal, Dev and Eve

screens.question: How many different rankings are possible?

options.why: You let the tied pair face two ways. Tied traders share one place, so there is no order inside the block.
You divided $5!$ by $2!$, as if Ana and Ben were identical letters. That also counts rankings with someone between them, but tied traders share one place.
You ranked all five as if nobody tied.

hints.text: A tie glues two traders into one place.
Inside a tie there is no first and second.
4 units in $4!$ orders, and the block has only 1 way.

feedback.correct: Four places to order, and the tie never flips: $4! = 24$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Treat the tie as one block, then ask whether it can face two ways.

byKey.divided: You divided $5!$ by $2!$, as if Ana and Ben were identical letters. That also counts rankings with someone between them, but tied traders share one place.

explain.text: The tie acts as a block that does not flip, so we order 4 units: $4! = 24$. On the seating screens the block faced 2 ways and doubled the count. Here dividing by $2!$ is right only after gluing: $\tfrac{4! \times 2!}{2!} = 24$.

ideas: Glue items that must sit together into one block, arrange the units, then arrange inside the block.
Kept apart is everything minus kept together.
Round a table with identical chairs, fix one person and arrange the rest: $(n-1)!$. Numbered seats make it a row again.

formula.name: Kept together in a row
formula.note: $k$ of $n$ items kept together as one block. Two items kept apart: $n! - 2\,(n-1)!$.

summary.trap: Divide for turns of the table only when the chairs are alike. Numbered seats make every turn a new plan.

quiz.prose: Six people sit in a row. Two of them, Kai and Lee, must sit side by side.
quiz.question: How many seatings are there?

options.why: You glued Kai and Lee but kept them in one order. The block faces 2 ways.
That is every seating, $6!$. Many of those split Kai and Lee.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Glue the pair, arrange the units, then flip the block.

explain.text: Gluing leaves 5 units in $5! = 120$ orders, and the block faces 2 ways. So there are $120 \times 2 = 240$ seatings.

quiz.prose: Six people sit at a round table with identical chairs. Turning everyone round the table gives the same seating.
quiz.question: How many different seatings are there?

feedback.correct: Fix one person, then arrange the other five: $5! = 120$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each round seating appears 6 times among the rows.

byKey.row: You counted rows. Each round seating appears 6 times, once per turn of the table.
byKey.mirror: You also divided by 2 for mirror images. A mirror image swaps left and right neighbours, so it is a new seating.

explain.text: The $6! = 720$ rows give each round seating 6 times. So there are $\tfrac{720}{6} = 5! = 120$.

quiz.prose: Six people sit in a row. Kai and Lee must not sit side by side.
quiz.question: How many seatings are there?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count every seating, then take away the together ones.

byKey.together: That is the together count. Subtract it from the total.
byKey.one-way: You took away 120, the block facing one way only. The together count is 240.
byKey.all: That is every seating. Some of them have Kai and Lee side by side.

explain.text: All seatings: $6! = 720$. Together: $5! \times 2 = 240$. So apart is $720 - 240 = 480$, which matches $(n-2)(n-1)! = 4 \times 120$.

quiz.prose: Four people sit at a round table with identical chairs. Ana and Ben must sit next to each other.
quiz.question: How many different seatings are there?

options.why: You used $3! \times 2!$, the count for a row. Round the table, 3 units have only $(3-1)! = 2$ orders.
You arranged the units round the table but kept the block in one order.
That is every round seating of four, $3!$. Some of them split Ana and Ben.

feedback.correct: Three units round a table, $2!$ ways, times 2 for the block.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Glue the pair, then seat 3 units round the table.

explain.text: Gluing leaves 3 units round the table: $(3-1)! = 2$ orders. The block faces 2 ways, so there are $2 \times 2 = 4$ seatings.
